biomarker_name.notes: No specific individual biomarker values (e.g., named biomarker with a discrete measured value) were reported in the main text; clinical parameters such as SBP/DBP/FBG were reported only as classification thresholds or P-values, not as biomarker measurements with paired values/units.

disease_response_os.notes: Study does not report survival outcomes; this is a microbiome/hypertension study, not an oncology survival study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status is not applicable to this hypertension/microbiome cohort study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: While the paper extensively discusses fecal microbiota composition (e.g., genera abundances, enterotypes), no field named 'feces_phenotype' with discrete numeric values was explicitly defined or reported as such in the text; extraction of these complex multi-genera abundance datasets is not feasible from the provided sections without fabricating structure.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this study concerns hypertension and gut microbiota, not tumors.

extraction_warnings: No per-subject or per-sample level data (age, sex, IDs) were reported in the main text; only aggregate cohort-level descriptions were available.

Sequencing platform for metagenomic (shotgun) data was only described as 'Illumina platform' without specifying HiSeq/MiSeq/etc.; the explicit 'Illumina HiSeq' designation applies to the 16S rRNA sequencing of transplanted mouse samples, not necessarily the human metagenomic cohort.
PMID and study_name are not stated within the paper body text; these were left as not_reported despite being available as external metadata.
Control/case designation for pHTN and HTN groups was inferred from group definitions rather than an explicit case/control label in the text.

Most schema fields (zygosity, age, BMI, HLA, neonatal/obgyn variables, tumor staging, disease response metrics) are not applicable to this hypertension/gut-microbiome cohort study and were not reported in the text.
Smoker and antibiotics_current_use values were inferred from exclusion criteria rather than directly stated participant status.
fmt_role and fmt_id are only partially described for human donors; mouse recipient identities are not itemized in the main text (see Additional file 11: Table S17).
disease/disease_details fields are subgroup-level (control/pHTN/HTN) based on blood-pressure classification criteria described in Methods.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['control', 'pHTN', 'HTN']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a gut microbiome/hypertension study, not an oncology or biomarker-panel clinical trial; most schema fields (biomarker_name/value/unit, disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size fields) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

The 'feces_phenotype_value' field could not be populated with discrete values because the paper reports complex multi-genera relative abundance data (e.g., Z-scores, box plots) rather than simple named phenotype-value pairs suitable for this schema without fabrication.

Host_species was inferred as human for the clinical cohort, though germ-free mice were also used in a separate transplantation experiment within the same study; only one value could be reported per the string type constraint.
